newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: S'pore telecom bidders unhurt by new licenses -TAS.
newsitem.headline: S'pore telecom bidders unhurt by new licenses -TAS.

text.p: The Telecommunication Authority of Singapore (TAS) said on Friday winners of licenses to operate basic telephone services in 2000 would not be hurt by plans to issue two more commercial phone services licenses in 2002.
TAS said in a statement that as license winners would be announced by mid-1998, the companies would have four years before new competitors came to the market.
This would give them "a reasonable and sufficient" time to roll out networks and build a client base adequate to withstand the arrival of competitors for commercial phone services.
Industry analysts say it takes about five years of competition-free operation for telephone companies to start to make decent profits.
TAS issued its statement after a meeting with three consortiums bidding for one or two licenses that will break Singapore Telecommunications' (SingTel's) monopoly on basic public phone services.

TAS called the meeting after it announced plans earlier this month to issue more licenses in 2002, catching tenderers off-guard and sparking complaints that business plans drawn up for their bids would be completely worthless.

TAS said it wanted "to provide certainty to the tenderers so that they can make their business cases taking future liberalisation moves into account", which is why it announced the 2002 licenses and called Friday's meeting.
"The briefing provided the tenderers with the necessary information for preparation of their main tender submissions," the statement said.
"They didn't tell us anything new," a spokeswoman for one consortium bidder, who declined to be identified, told Reuters.
"Today's conversation was more about interconnectivity. There will be more meetings about the bids, but these will have to be in private and not when all the rivals are in the same room," she said.
"There is still more to talk about," another consortium member told Reuters immediately after the meeting.
Some consortium members have said in the wake of the 2002 license news that they want to revise original submissions that qualified them as license tenderers.
Bidders can submit written enquiries about the tender at any time before a December 31, 1997 deadline, but TAS has not given any indication that total revision would be allowed.
The consortiums group state-run Singapore Technologies group, Singapore Power, Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp and British Telcommunications plc under the StarHub banner.
TelecomOne groups Singapore Press Holdings Ltd, Keppel Telecom, Cable & Wireless plc and Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd.
The third consortium links SembCorp, Singapore Mass Rapid Transit and Worldcom Inc.
